medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
We are committed to the well-being and success of all community members. Columbia complies with all applicable civil rights laws and does not engage in illegal preferences or discrimination.

OSDIB at the Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons (VP&S) was established in 1968 to recruit and nurture a diverse student body.

Through various student organizations and activities, VP&S and the entire CUIMC community enjoys tremendous interactions with its student body, distinguished faculty, and patient population.

Contact: 
Office of Student Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging
Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons
104 Haven Avenue, Suite 1003
New York, NY 10032
Phone (212) 305-4157
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The VP&S Club is a comprehensive student activities organization. Founded by Nobel Peace Laureate John R. Mott in 1894, the VP&S Club currently encompasses approximately 70 extracurricular organizations. These organizations represent VP&S students' vast interests and talents, including athletics, the performing arts, student advocacy, and community service. By providing VP&S students with outlets for their various talents, the VP&S Club adds substantial depth to a program otherwise devoted to scientific and clinical disciplines.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located in the Washington Heights neighborhood of New York City, the CUIMC is on a large multi-acre campus.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On campus housing is available for single students, married couples, and domestic partners.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: VP&S fosters a culture that values and supports all individuals. There is a faculty liaison for Lambda, a student group supporting LGBTQ+ students, and several student clubs serving gender and sexual minority groups including: Q Clinic, Association of Women’s Surgeons, and American Medical Women’s Association. All students are welcome to participate.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
Disability Services, part of Student Health Services at Columbia University Irving Medical Center (CUIMC), facilitates equal access for students with disabilities by coordinating reasonable accommodations and support, including for temporary injuries and illnesses. Columbia Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons has a Disability Services liaison to assist our students with related requests.

Accommodations may include adjustments to policies, practices, and procedures to support student success without lessening academic or programmatic requirements. Examples include note-taking services, exam administration, ASL interpreters, assistive technology, and coordination of accessible housing, with services determined based on a student’s needs, documentation, and program requirements.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
VP&S offers numerous wellness resources for our students ranging from counseling services to well-being and health promotion programs.  

During each core clerkship, students also receive a half-day which they can use for wellness activities. The day is intended to promote well-being and self-care. 

For information regarding resources available to students, please visit: https://www.studenthealth.cuimc.columbia.edu/outreach-and-programs/well-being-and-health-promotion-programs
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The Columbia University Irving Medical Center is a diverse, academic community of more than 10,000 students, faculty, and staff from across the nation and the world, living and learning on a dynamic campus in a great, global city. 

We foster community by supporting students in the development of skills and awareness of self and others required to responsibly engage, serve and lead at Columbia, in New York City and beyond.

Our goal is for students to feel at home as part of the Columbia University community. To this end, faculty and administrative staff work together to create a student-centered experience.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to be clean, well groomed, and dressed in a manner appropriate to their responsibilities.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Deans for Student Affairs and Career Services offer walk-in hours for all students throughout the academic year.  The Student Success Network provides tutoring for the preclinical curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students are introduced to essential aspects of effective and compassionate patient care from the beginning of medical school through lectures, small-group seminars, and clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: The Major Clinical Year begins after the completion of 18 months of Fundamentals.  Two week-long intercessions called Mechanisms & Practice take place during the year of Clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: VP&S requires attendance and active participation in all components of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons curriculum is an innovative and flexible curriculum that recognizes the academic structure of medical education by dispensing with the old designations of first, second, third and fourth years. Those categories are replaced by three major segments in the curriculum: Fundamentals, Major Clinical Year, and Differentiation & Integration. Fundamentals focuses on the science of health and disease and on building clinical skills. The Major Clinical Year offers a survey of medical specialties in urban and rural settings. Differentiation & Integration provides advanced clinical training and an in-depth scholarly project. The curriculum balances scientific rigor with patient-centered care.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
VP&S balances exposure to primary care and specialty care.

In the first semester, students are placed at sites for clerkships, working with physicians, nurses, social workers, physical therapists and other members of the health care team. 

During MCY, all students complete training in family medicine or internal medicine primary care.  In this required clerkship, students are sent to geographically and socioeconomically diverse communities. Students also have the option to gain experiences in rural farming communities, veterans’ health and Native American primary care through IHS sites. 

In addition, students receive training in ambulatory pediatrics and women’s health services.  Many students participate in one of the five student-run and faculty-supervised free clinics. 

Finally, the Daniel Noyes Brown Primary Care Scholars Program is a structured four year longitudinal experience in primary care which provides mentorship and increased primary care exposure to students.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
There are numerous opportunities for students to engage in research at all levels. The summer between first and second year as well as during the Scholarly Project and elective months are ideal times to explore. In addition, students may opt to become involved during the three semesters of the Fundamentals curriculum.
 
VP&S also offers a dual degree for matriculated medical students: the MD/Masters in Biomedical Sciences (MD/MS).  This program reflects VP&S’s commitment to develop clinicians who will be leaders in advancing medical research, practice, policy and education. By integrating research training with medical education, this program enhances the research skills of students and provides several opportunities to pursue research interests with faculty research mentors. Areas of research focus may include basic/translational science, biomedical informatics, clinical research, global and population health, medical education, narrative and social medicine and precision medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A four month long Scholarly Project is required during D&I.  Additional research projects are often pursued by VP&S students.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: NewYork-Presbyterian is our major teaching hospital.  Major affiliates include Harlem Hospital Center in Manhattan; Bassett Hospital in Cooperstown, NY; and Stamford Hospital in Connecticut.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons (VP&S) was founded in 1767 and conferred the first Doctor of Medicine degree in the North American Colonies in 1770. 
Throughout our history, we have upheld the belief: "Of the Most High Cometh Healing." Major affiliates include Harlem Hospital Center in Manhattan, Bassett Healthcare in Cooperstown, NY, and Stamford Hospital in Connecticut.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
“We aspire to transform human health by driving discovery, advancing care, and educating leaders.” We do this work in service to others and our community, both locally and globally. 

The mission of the VP&S MD program also includes the following statements: 

We are committed to fostering an environment that values civility, acceptance, respect, ethics, and support (CUIMC CARES), ensuring that our staff, faculty, and students have meaningful opportunities to put these values into action. 

At VP&S, we strive to educate the next generation of physician leaders who will serve neighboring, national, and global communities through the lens of health equity, promoting both well-being and state-of-the-art care of patients. 

Experiences at VP&S will shape the future and set the standards for medicine throughout the United States and globally. Guided exposure and training will exhibit the highest principles of humanism and professionalism in their responsibilities to their patients, to their community, and to society.

The values of humanism, collaboration, inquiry, transformation, growth, and wellness—both individually and collectively—inspire our every effort in pursuit of this goal.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: We welcome letters of recommendation from individuals and premedical advisory groups (Committee Letters) with genuine knowledge of applicants and their capabilities, who can provide more than routine praise. Our admissions committee requires three letters of recommendation and accepts up to seven. One must come from a science faculty member, teacher, or research mentor.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Please note the following information regarding coursework: The Admissions Committee at Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons has voted to accept Pass/Fail grades for prerequisite courses taken at schools that decided to go Pass/Fail for the 2020 academic calendar and Spring/Summer 2021 semesters. We understand some concerns about the impact on GPAs and will take this fully into consideration for future applicants. For students in schools for which Pass/Fail is optional during those semesters, we will consider each student’s situation individually.

For information regarding policies and the admissions process please visit:
https://www.ps.columbia.edu/education/academic-programs/md-program/admissions/apply-md-program
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are required but one consideration of our comprehensive review.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We do not have a  minimum undergraduate GPA to consider an applicant's postbacc or graduate coursework.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo:
We do not have credit hour requirements but do have the requirement of:

One year of English or other writing-intensive courses.

One year of Biology with labs.

One year of Physics with one semester of a lab.

Two years of Chemistry, one of which must be Organic 
Chemistry, both with labs.

One semester of biochemistry, lab recommended but not required.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community college courses are accepted for students who transferred into a four-year institution. Community college credits are also accepted for students who have obtained a bachelor's degree and lack one or two of the required courses.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We accept letters uploaded through the secondary application portal.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Candidates for admission must review and verify their ability to meet the VP&S technical standards when completing the application for admission.  Candidates will be evaluated on a case-by-case individualized basis regarding their eligibility for admission, a process that examines and values all of the skills, attitudes, and attributes deemed necessary to safely and successfully complete the MD program. All candidates for admission, both those with and without disabilities, are expected to be competitive with others in the applicant pool with respect to academic, personal, and extracurricular achievements. In addition, we will review and verify with students at each curriculum phase transition (Fundamentals to Major Clinical Year and again at the start at Differentiation and Intergration).

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Admission is not based on an applicant's ability to pay. We make every effort to help accepted students finance their medical education. In 2017 we became the first medical school in the nation to meet 100 percent of demonstrated financial need with scholarships for all students who qualify.  Approximately $21 million in need-based scholarships has been awarded for 2025-26. To be considered, financial data for student, spouse and parents must be provided. Federal and private student loan programs are available to cover educational expenses that cannot be met by family resources. Students who do not qualify for need-based funds from the school can access the Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loan and private educational loans. Students in Columbia's Bassett track also receive separate scholarship support.  More information is available on our website: http://ps.columbia.edu/financialaid.

medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq:
* A PhD in one of the biological or related sciences from an accredited US or Canadian school
* An intention to pursue biomedical research as a physician scientist
* A record supporting exceptional scientific promise
* US citizenship or permanent resident status

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The waitlist is not ranked and remains open until the first day of class.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
At the time of application, at least three full academic years at an accredited college in the U.S. or Canada. 

One year of English or other writing-intensive courses.

One year of Biology with labs.

One year of Physics with one semester of a lab.

Two years of Chemistry, one of which must be Organic 
Chemistry, both with labs.

One semester of biochemistry, lab recommended but not required.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: All prerequisite courses must have been completed within ten years of the application cycle. We prefer that the prerequisite courses in biology be taken within five years of the application cycle.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: We seek applicants who have shown the greatest evidence of excellence and leadership potential in the science and art of medicine. Beyond academic ability, medicine also demands integrity, the ability to relate to others and have concern for their welfare. The school evaluates applicants by several means: academic achievement, letters of recommendation, participation in extracurricular and summer activities, breadth of interests, and the personal interviews. Admission is possible for all qualified applicants regardless of sex, race, age, religion, sexual orientation, or national origin.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Although shadowing is not required, the experience is an effective method of getting familiar with the field of medicine. Shadowing will provide you with clinical exposure, physician and patient interaction as well as an opportunity to learn further about health systems.
